# WebKit

<!-- generated:header (isim/tools/coverage-summary.py; do not edit by hand) -->
**Symbols:** 80.8% of Apple's iOS API (915 of 1132, exact) · **Rows:** 18: 13 ✅ 2 🟡 3 ❌ · **iOS:** 16.0+
<!-- /generated:header -->

**Area:** [Web, network & communication](../COVERAGE.md#web) · **Apple:** [WebKit](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/webkit) · **Issues:** [`area:web`](https://github.com/kolabs-dev/isim/issues?q=is%3Aissue+is%3Aopen+label%3Aarea%3Aweb)

## How isim implements it

- **Passthrough:** WebKitGTK 6.0 in a helper process (`isim-webkit`). isim draws the pixels; the Objective-C names sit over the Swift overlay.

## API

| API / feature | Status | iOS | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| WebKit `WKWebView` rendering and loading (`load`, `loadHTMLString`, `loadFileURL`, `load(_:mimeType:…)`, back/forward, reload, KVO `title`/`url`/`isLoading`/`estimatedProgress`/`canGoBack`) | ✅ | ≤17 | real WebKit: the host's WebKitGTK 6.0 in a helper process (`isim-webkit`, private invisible broadway display) renders frames at the screen scale; iOS-style user agent; history includes `loadHTMLString` pages. Adapted: `load` sends GET + headers only. A page without `<meta name=viewport>` lays out 980 CSS px wide and is scaled to fit the view, as on iOS (isim decides as the page is parsed; tested: test_web_extras). Needs `webkitgtk-6.0` + `gtk4-broadwayd` on the host (else a placeholder and a failed navigation). Tested (HelloWeb) |
| WebKit delegates (`WKNavigationDelegate` action/response policy, start/commit/finish/fail; `WKUIDelegate` alert/confirm/prompt, `createWebViewWith`) | ✅ | ≤17 | completion and async forms; cancelled links; JavaScript panels through the app's UI delegate (none → dismissed like iOS). App Transport Security: a cleartext navigation or redirect the app's Info.plist does not allow (`NSAllowsArbitraryLoadsInWebContent`, exception domains, local networking) is cancelled after the action policy and fails provisionally with -1022 (HelloTransportSecurity); subresources inside the page are not filtered. Tested; `createWebViewWith`, process termination unverified |
| WebKit JavaScript bridge (`evaluateJavaScript`, `callAsyncJavaScript`, content worlds, `WKUserScript`, `WKScriptMessageHandler`(`WithReply`), `WKURLSchemeHandler`) | ✅ | ≤17 | results converted like iOS (dictionaries, arrays, numbers, `WKError.javaScriptExceptionOccurred`, unsupported types); isolated worlds; replies to page promises, including dictionaries and arrays: adapted, because WebKitGTK cannot hand a page an object made in the UI process, so isim sends them as JSON text, which a script in the handler's world turns back into objects before the promise resolves (#828). Tested (HelloWeb: test_web) |
| WebKit input, selection, scrolling, zoom, menus, find, PDF, web archives, website data (`WKWebsiteDataStore`, `WKHTTPCookieStore`), snapshots | ✅ | ≤17 | adapted input: taps, typing (system keyboard on focused fields) and scrolling become DOM events from an isolated world (`isTrusted` false); `scrollView` mirrors page scrolling. A long press selects a word (selection tint and handles, edit menu with Copy / Select All / Share…, `copy:` / `selectAll:`); a long press on a link or image opens a context menu with a live preview (`WKUIDelegate` `contextMenuConfigurationFor`, will-present, did-end, commit; else Open / Copy Link / Share…); `<select>` and `<select multiple>` become UIKit menus (option groups, disabled options, change events); pinch zoom within the viewport meta's scales (`user-scalable=no` honoured), `scrollView.zoomScale` follows; `isFindInteractionEnabled` / `findInteraction` (find navigator, highlights, n of m); `createPDF` (whole page or `WKPDFConfiguration.rect`, WebKit's print backend at CSS size, cropped with poppler) and `createWebArchiveData` (WebKit's MHTML as a webarchive plist: main resource and subresources). Cookies get/set/delete and data removal; `takeSnapshot`. Tested (test_web, test_web_interact) |
| SwiftUI `WebView` / `WebPage` (iOS 26) | ✅ | 26.0 | on WKWebView: `WebPage` is `@Observable` (`title`, `url`, `isLoading`, `estimatedProgress`, `currentNavigationEvent`), `load` (request, HTML, data) returning the navigation events as an `AsyncSequence`, `reload`, `callJavaScript` with arguments, `pdf`, `snapshot`, `webArchiveData`, `find`, `URLSchemeHandler`; `WebView(page)` / `WebView(url:)` with `webViewBackForwardNavigationGestures`, `webViewLinkPreviews`, `webViewMagnificationGestures`, `webViewContentBackground`. Tested (HelloWeb -webpage, test_web_webpage) |
| Authentication challenges: `WKNavigationDelegate.webView(_:didReceive:completionHandler:)` (and `respondTo` async) | ✅ | ≤17 | passthrough of WebKitGTK's `authenticate` signal: HTTP Basic, Digest, NTLM and Negotiate become a `URLAuthenticationChallenge` (`URLProtectionSpace` with host, port, realm, method; `previousFailureCount`; the proposed user); `.useCredential` hands WebKit the credential with its persistence, `.performDefaultHandling` and `.rejectProtectionSpace` continue without credentials (the server's 401 page, as on iOS), `.cancelAuthenticationChallenge` cancels the load; no delegate method: the 401 page. `URLSession.AuthChallengeDisposition` is now `@objc` (`NSURLSessionAuthChallengeDisposition`) so Objective-C delegates get it; apps built before keep their enum-case symbols (`swift/overlays/Foundation/compat.c`). Tested (HelloWeb -transfers: test_web_transfers) |
| Downloads: `WKDownload` (`originalRequest`, `webView`, `delegate`, `progress`, `isUserInitiated`, `originatingFrame`, `cancel(_:)`), `WKDownloadDelegate` (destination, redirect, challenge, finish, failure with resume data), `WKWebView.startDownload(using:completionHandler:)`, `resumeDownload(fromResumeData:completionHandler:)`, `.download` action and response policies with `navigationAction` / `navigationResponse` `didBecome download` | ✅ | ≤17 | passthrough of WebKitGTK's downloads (the web view's session: cookies, credentials), saved where the delegate's destination says; `progress` follows the received bytes. Adapted: WebKitGTK cannot resume a partial download, so isim's resume data (the URL and destination) restarts it to the same file; `cancel(_:)` hands the resume data to its handler and the delegate hears only of other failures; a `data:` URL is suggested as "Unknown" with its type's extension, like Safari. WebKitGTK cannot download from a custom scheme (`WKURLSchemeHandler`). The completion-handler and async forms of the destination method are both optional (on iOS the completion form is required). Tested (HelloWeb -transfers; HelloWebObjC) |
| Camera and microphone: `WKUIDelegate.webView(_:requestMediaCapturePermissionFor:initiatedByFrame:type:decisionHandler:)` (and async), `WKMediaCaptureType`, `WKPermissionDecision` | ✅ | ≤17 | `getUserMedia` asks the UI delegate: `.grant`, `.deny`, or `.prompt` (also without the method) shows iOS's alert, “Allow “host” to use your camera?” (Don’t Allow / Allow). Adapted: the page gets WebKit's mock camera and microphone (a test pattern), as isim's web engine has no capture devices. Tested (HelloWeb -transfers: the alert, Allow, a video track) |
| Content rule lists: `WKContentRuleListStore` (`default()`, `init(url:)`, compile / look up / remove / `getAvailableContentRuleListIdentifiers`, completion and async forms), `WKContentRuleList`, `WKUserContentController.add(_:)` / `remove(_:)` / `removeAllContentRuleLists()` | ✅ | ≤17 | passthrough: the web engine compiles Apple's JSON rules with WebKitGTK's content filters (`WebKitUserContentFilterStore`, the same WebKit rule compiler) into the store's directory (the app's `Library/WebKit/ContentRuleLists` by default); a list added to a controller applies to its web views at once (`block`, `css-display-none`, `ignore-previous-rules`, `make-https`, `block-cookies`, triggers with `url-filter`, `if-domain`, `resource-type`, `load-type`); invalid JSON fails with `WKError.contentRuleListStoreCompileFailed`, a missing identifier with `contentRuleListStoreLookUpFailed`. Tested (HelloWeb `-rules`, tests/ui/test_web.py::test_web_content_rules) |
| WebKit from Objective-C (`#import <WebKit/WebKit.h>`, `WKWebView` by its Objective-C name) | ✅ | ≤17 | adapted: Objective-C headers over the Swift overlay's classes (Apple's class names and selectors, delegates, KVO, subclasses and categories from Objective-C, `evaluateJavaScript:`/`callAsyncJavaScript:` and the other completion-handler APIs, `WKURLSchemeHandler` / `WKURLSchemeTask`, `WKDownload` / `WKDownloadDelegate`, `startDownloadUsingRequest:`, the challenge, download and media capture delegate methods). Tested: test_web_objc (HelloWebObjC); runs Google Mobile Ads ([#200](https://github.com/kolabs-dev/isim/issues/200)) |
| `WKWebView.fullscreenState` (`WKFullscreenState`, KVO) and element fullscreen | ✅ | 16.0 | adapted: with `WKPreferences.isElementFullscreenEnabled`, an element's `requestFullscreen()` presents the web view full screen (black, no status bar, a close button, `isim-web-fullscreen-close`), as iOS does; the state goes entering → in → exiting → not in. WebKitGTK's fullscreen signals; without the preference `requestFullscreen()` is refused. Tested (HelloWeb `-extras`, tests/ui/test_web.py `test_web_extras`, `os_matrix`; HelloWebObjC) |
| File inputs: `WKOpenPanelParameters`, `WKUIDelegate.webView(_:runOpenPanelWith:initiatedByFrame:completionHandler:)` | ✅ | 18.4 | passthrough of WebKitGTK's file chooser request: the delegate's URLs become the `<input type=file>`'s files (`change` fires), nil cancels it (`cancel` fires). Without the method (and before iOS 18.4) the web view shows iOS's menu: Photo Library (isim's photo picker), Take Photo or Video (when a camera is simulated), Choose File (the document picker). Adapted: `allowsDirectories` is always false (WebKitGTK does not say). Tested (HelloWeb `-extras`: test_web_extras, `os_matrix`) |
| Web extensions: `WKWebExtension` (`init(resourceBaseURL:)`, `init(appExtensionBundle:)`, the manifest, display names and versions localised from `_locales`, permissions and host permissions, `allRequestedMatchPatterns`, the `has…` flags, `icon(for:)`, `actionIcon(for:)`, `errors`, `Error`, `Permission`), `WKWebExtension.MatchPattern` (`Options`, `Error`), `WKWebExtensionController` (`Configuration`, `load(_:)`, `unload(_:)`, `extensionContexts`, `extensions`, `extensionContext(for:)`), `WKWebExtensionContext` (granted and denied permissions and match patterns with expiration dates, `permissionStatus(for:)`, `setPermissionStatus(_:for:expirationDate:)`, `hasAccess(to:)`, `hasInjectedContent(for:)`, `optionsPageURL`, `Error`, `PermissionStatus`), `WKWebViewConfiguration.webExtensionController` | 🟡 | 18.4 | adapted: WebKitGTK has no browser-extension runtime. isim reads manifest versions 2 and 3, and a loaded context's content scripts and CSS (`matches`, `exclude_matches`, `run_at`, `all_frames`) run in the controller's web views, in a content world of their own, on pages the context was granted, with `browser.*` (the row below). Tested (HelloWeb `-extras`: test_web_extras; HelloWebObjC: test_web_objc) |
| Web extension tabs, windows and runtime: `WKWebExtensionTab`, `WKWebExtensionWindow` (completion-handler and async forms), `WKWebExtension.TabConfiguration`, `.WindowConfiguration`, `.TabChangedProperties`, `.WindowType`, `.WindowState`; `WKWebExtensionControllerDelegate` (open windows, focused window, new tabs and windows, options page, permission prompts, `didUpdate` action, action popups, native messages, message ports) and `WKWebExtensionController.delegate`; `WKWebExtension.Action` (`label`, `badgeText`, `hasUnreadBadgeText`, `icon(for:)`, `isEnabled`, `menuItems`, `presentsPopup`, `popupWebView`, `popupViewController`, `closePopup()`), `WKWebExtension.Command` (`id`, `title`, `activationKey`, `modifierFlags`, `menuItem`, `keyCommand`), `WKWebExtension.MessagePort` (`Error`), `WKWebExtension.DataRecord` (`Error`), `WKWebExtension.DataType`; the context's and the controller's `did…` tab and window events, `openTabs`, `openWindows`, `focusedWindow`, `action(for:)`, `performAction(for:)`, `commands`, `performCommand(_:)`, `performCommand(for:)`, `menuItems(for:)`, `hasPermission(_:in:)`, `hasAccess(to:in:)`, `permissionStatus(for:in:)`, `userGesturePerformed(in:)`, `hasActiveUserGesture(in:)`, `clearUserGesture(in:)`, `loadBackgroundContent(completionHandler:)`, the permission notifications and `NotificationUserInfoKey`; `allExtensionDataTypes`, `fetchDataRecords(ofTypes:)`, `fetchDataRecord(ofTypes:for:)`, `removeData(ofTypes:from:)` | 🟡 | 18.4 | adapted: isim runs the extension itself. The background page, scripts or service worker run in a hidden web view on `webkit-extension://<uniqueIdentifier>/`, which serves the extension's files (also for popups and pages shown with the context's `webViewConfiguration`). `browser.*` / `chrome.*` reach the context through a script message handler. Content scripts get `runtime` (`id`, `getManifest`, `getURL`, `sendMessage`, `onMessage`), `storage` and `i18n`. Extension pages also get `runtime.sendNativeMessage` / `connectNative` / `openOptionsPage` / `onInstalled`, `tabs`, `windows`, `scripting` (`executeScript`, `insertCSS`, `removeCSS`), `action`, `commands`, `menus` and `permissions`. Tabs, windows, popups, prompts and native messaging are the app's, through the protocols and the delegate. A user gesture grants `activeTab`. `storage.local` / `sync` are saved under Library/WebKit/WebExtensions (in memory for a non-persistent controller) and are the extension's data records. Not on isim: `declarativeNetRequest`, `webRequest`, `webNavigation`, `alarms`, `cookies`, `runtime.connect` between extension parts, service-worker-only APIs, and extension resources in the app's own web views. Tested (HelloWeb `-extension`: test_web_extension_runtime; HelloWebObjC: test_web_objc) |
